newsitem.title: USA: U.S. natural gas supplies set for winter - EIA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. natural gas supplies set for winter - EIA.

text.p: There is no shortage of natural gas for this winter, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said on Monday.
U.S. production of natural gas is expected to rise to 53.0 billion cubic feet a day in October through March from 51.1 Bcf a day last winter.
Stock drawdowns of natural gas are expected to average 10.2 Bcf a day, down from 11.5 Bcf a day last winter.
Net imports are projected to average 8.5 Bcf a day, up 1.0 Bcf from last winter, on the assumption that imports will be more available during a normal winter, EIA said.
Retail natural gas prices are expected to average $6.10 per thousand cubic feet through the winter, up about 7 cents from last winter.
